subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@atlas-payments.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 15:02:10 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Hi Amit / Sofia —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the proposed POC/trial plan and suggested success criteria so we can align on scope and owners before we spin up resources. I attached a quick draft spreadsheet with the KPI table.

POC overview (3-week trial):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for payments NLP pipeline (fraud intent classification + entity extraction) under production-like load.
- Timeline: Week 0 (prep), Week 1 (baseline + integration), Week 2 (load / latency tuning), Week 3 (quality evaluation + wrap).

Success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 300ms (including network) for 90% of requests; p99 < 600ms as a stretch goal.
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/sec with steady-state CPU/GPU utilization < 75% on dedicated pool.
- Cost: model cost/token <= $0.002 (target) when using batching and caching.
- Quality: classification F1 >= 0.92 on your labeled eval set; entity extraction exact match >= 0.90.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and graceful fallback to smaller model for >99.9% of calls.

Owners / responsibilities:
- Atlas: provide representative eval dataset (10k labeled samples) + any privacy constraints; Amit to own.
- Redwood SE: test harness, load script, staging endpoint; Marissa to own.
- Redwood AE: coordination, timing, contracting; I (Jordan) to own.

Next steps:
1) Amit: confirm the dataset availability and any redaction requirements — target by Mon 10/12.
2) Marissa: I'll loop you on infra details; can you provide the staging endpoint and test-harness checklist by Tue 10/13?
3) Jordan: I'll send a short mutual action plan + access request after we confirm dataset.

Attachments: POC_success_criteria_draft.xlsx (kpi table + timeline).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com]

From: Amit Shah <amit@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:18:30 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches my notes. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset: We can provide ~12k labeled transactions across the fraud/intent classes you saw. We'll need to redact PANs and full card numbers — is tokenization acceptable? We'll try to have the first pass ready by Monday 10/12.
2) Latency measurement: When you say p95 end-to-end, are you measuring from our client to the response or server-side only? We want to ensure the SLA reflects our integration overhead.
3) Cost: The $0.002/token target looks reasonable as a goal — curious how batching assumptions affect that number.

Also can you share the test harness spec and any network infographic (eg egress requirements / port lists) so our infra team can pre-approve?

If we can get those clarifications, I think we can lock in the timeline and kick off next week.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of ML Platform | Atlas Payments
amit@atlas-payments.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@atlas-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Thanks — adding a few technical details and what we'll measure from the Redwood side.

Measurement approach:
- Latency: we report both server-side (inference start -> response sent) and client-observed (round-trip from your test harness) p50/p95/p99. For SLA purposes we'll highlight client-observed p95. We'll include warmup runs (5k requests) and then measure steady-state over 15 minutes.
- Throughput: we'll run controlled load tests (ramp to target) and report sustained throughput with GPU utilization. We'll also test with and without KV cache priming to show gains.
- Cost/token: our estimate assumes batching at avg batch size ~6 and prefix caching; we'll provide a cost sensitivity table in the attachment.
- Quality: please provide the labeled eval set (CSV with id, text, label(s)) — we'll run evaluation on the same splits you use locally and provide confusion matrices + examples of failures.

Integration / infra notes:
- We'll provision a staging endpoint for Atlas in your preferred region. Staging endpoint: https://console.redwood.ai/projects/atlas-payments/poc (internal link).
- Network: outbound HTTPS egress on 443; minimal inbound port requirements. See attached network_requirements.pdf for details.

Attachments: network_requirements.pdf (1 page), cost_sensitivity.csv (attached inline).

If this looks good, I'll provision the staging endpoint and share credentials + a quick runbook. Jordan — if you want, I can draft the mutual action plan in HubSpot once Amit confirms dataset availability.

— Marissa
